symptom: ako/mxcli#1782 (mendixlabs/mxcli#1676): "`mxcli debug break` prints \"Breakpoint set\" but the runtime never registers the breakpoint" — the microflow runs to the end; a logging proxy showed add_breakpoint sent without `condition` and answered {"message":"Missing property: condition","status":2}. Same session: `debug inspect <var>` printed {} for a String variable, `debug continue` after a step printed "Continued." while the flow stayed paused until `continue --all`, and some debug calls seemed to hang while a flow was paused
cause: The /debugger/ endpoint answers every request with HTTP 200 and reports the outcome in the envelope: {"result":…,"status":0} on success, {"result":{},"message":…,"status":2} on a refusal (every reply measured on 11.13 and 11.15). DebuggerClient.post checked only the HTTP status, so every refusal came back as success with an empty result — and three malformed requests stayed invisible behind it: add_breakpoint omitted `condition` when empty (required: "Missing property: condition"), `continue` sent {} (required debug_id: "Missing property: debug_id"), and `inspect` sent a primitive to get_object, which takes objects only ("The variable 'Greeting' is not a Mendix object."). The 'hang' is poll_events, a long poll that returns after ~25 s when no event is pending, called by every paused/step/inspect/continue that auto-resolves the flow
file: `cmd/mxcli/docker/debugger.go` (`post`, `DebuggerError`, `AddBreakpoint`, `Continue`/`ContinueAll`); `cmd/mxcli/cmd_debug.go` (`continue --flow`, inspect of a primitive, SilenceUsage in RunE); `cmd/mxcli/debug_resolve.go` (`pausedVariable`)
insight: An API that puts the outcome in the body turns a status-code-only client into one where every refusal is a success, and then each malformed request it sends is invisible: one missing envelope check hid three protocol bugs. Surface the envelope first; the other bugs then fail on their own (the existing continue test went red the moment the stub answered like the runtime). The wrong turn is the proposal's protocol table (`condition?`, `continue {}`): it was never read against the envelope. Probe the runtime directly — a 30-line client posting each action through a logging proxy — and keep the stub answering the runtime's way (status, plus a 'Missing property' refusal per required param); the old stub replied {"result":{}} to everything, so the tests passed against a protocol that does not exist. Not fixed, both measured: poll_events consumes events, and an event delivered to an abandoned poll (client timeout, a `timeout` wrapper) is lost — a short poll timeout is NOT a safe fix for the 25 s wait (control: with no poll in flight the same pause's event arrives); and queued paused_microflow events outlive the pause (one for a finished flow came back minutes later). Controls: stubbing the status guard fails 17 tests with 'the client reported success'; the pre-fix binary prints 'Breakpoint set' and exits 0 for a condition the runtime refuses
